# glinet_wifi_iface (Resource)

Manages a Wi-Fi interface (a Wi-Fi network) of the router, for example the main 5 GHz network `default_radio0` or the guest network `guest2g` (`wifi.set_config` in the router API). Use one instance of this resource for each interface. The interface always exists on the router, so create takes over the interface. The web UI writes the switch (`enabled`) and the other attributes in two calls. The provider sends a call only when one of its values differs: on create from the values of the router, on update from the state. A create whose values are equal to those of the router sends no write. When it disables an interface, the provider sends the switch first; else it sends the switch last. This resource does not manage the radio (channel, channel width, hardware mode, TX power): for a main interface, the web UI also sends `device`, `hwmode`, `txpower` and `random_bssid` of the radio, so the provider reads them from the router just before the write and sends them back unchanged. It does not send `channel` and `htmode`, as the web UI does while the repeater uses the radio. **Danger:** a write can restart the Wi-Fi of the radio, which disconnects its clients; it is not known whether it also restarts the other radio. When the uplink of the router is a Wi-Fi repeater on the same radio, a write can cut the uplink. A write to the LAN configuration (`glinet_lan_config`) restarted the Wi-Fi of a GL-AXT1800 with firmware 4.7.0 and cut its repeater uplink until a reboot; a Wi-Fi write can probably do the same. The write of this resource was not tested on a router; the parameters come from the router's web UI. Destroy removes the resource from the Terraform state and does not change the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "guest_wifi_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "glinet_wifi_iface" "guest" {
  name       = "guest5g"
  ssid       = "guest"
  encryption = "sae-mixed"
  key        = var.guest_wifi_key
  enabled    = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the interface is enabled (`enabled` in the router API).
- `encryption` (String) Encryption (`encryption` in the router API): `none` (open), `psk2` (WPA2-PSK), `psk-mixed` (WPA/WPA2-PSK), `sae` (WPA3-SAE) or `sae-mixed` (WPA2-PSK/WPA3-SAE). The router lists the encryptions that each radio supports; create and update fail when the radio does not support the value.
- `name` (String) Name of the interface on the router, for example `default_radio0`, `guest5g`, `default_radio1` or `guest2g` (`iface_name` in the router API). Changing it replaces the resource.
- `ssid` (String) Name of the Wi-Fi network, 1 to 32 bytes (`ssid` in the router API).

### Optional

- `hidden` (Boolean) Whether the network name is hidden (`hidden` in the router API). Defaults to `false`.
- `key` (String, Sensitive) Wi-Fi password (`key` in the router API): 8 to 63 printable ASCII characters, or 64 hex digits; at most 63 characters for `sae` and `sae-mixed`. Required unless `encryption` is `none`, and cannot be set then.

### Read-Only

- `band` (String) Band of the radio, for example `5G` or `2G` (`band` in the router API).
- `guest` (Boolean) Whether the interface is a guest network (`guest` in the router API).
- `radio` (String) Device name of the radio, for example `radio0` (`device` in the router API).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the name of the Wi-Fi interface on the router.
terraform import glinet_wifi_iface.guest guest5g
```
